entities.summary:
The Libertarian Party of the United States, founded in 1971 in David Nolan's home in Colorado Springs, is the third-largest political party in America and the world's most significant libertarian political organization — advocating for minimal government intervention in economic and personal life, drug legalization, non-interventionist foreign policy, and civil liberties protection across political spectrum. The Libertarian Party's 2016 campaign under Gary Johnson (who received 4.5 million votes — 3.28% — the best Libertarian performance in history) demonstrated third-party potential in American politics.

The party was founded by David Nolan and colleagues opposed to both the Nixon administration's domestic expansion and the Vietnam War — a combination of free-market economics and anti-war civil libertarianism. The party's platform consistently advocates marijuana legalization, same-sex marriage, gun rights, and drug decriminalization — positions that cross traditional left-right boundaries. Libertarian candidates often draw votes from both Republicans (fiscal conservatives) and Democrats (civil libertarians).

The Libertarian Party's most significant policy contribution is the mainstreaming of marijuana legalization: Libertarian advocacy since 1972 contributed to the social acceptability that led 22 states to legalize recreational marijuana by 2024. Gary Johnson's 2016 performance (strongest third-party showing since Ross Perot) demonstrated that anti-establishment frustration could fuel a 4-5% third-party showing even in America's winner-take-all electoral system.
